Build PHASE 2 of "Sitewave" (the productized web-design agency) inside the Nxeon platform (/opt/nxeon, Next.js App Router + Prisma + Postgres). Phase 1 already shipped (branch merged to main): models Agency* (AgencyVertical/Template/Prospect/DemoSite/GenerationLog), lib/agency/{schema,generate,render,templates,config}.ts, admin "Agency" nav section with /admin/agency/{,verticals,prospects,demos}, lib/actions-agency.ts, preview route app/api/agency/demo/[id]/preview. Read those first to extend them, plus /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/projects/agency/architecture.md and board.json ("Backlog"/"Later" columns).

Branch `feature/agency-sitewave-phase2` off main (main is at 7f7a758). Commit + `git push -u origin feature/agency-sitewave-phase2`. Do NOT commit to main, do NOT deploy, do NOT `prisma db push`, do NOT edit .env. `npx prisma generate` + `npm run build` MUST pass 0 errors; add tests.

=== HARD GUARDRAILS ===
- The scrape pipeline is OPERATOR-TRIGGERED only (runs when an admin clicks "scrape & generate" on a specific prospect) — it must NEVER auto-crawl lists. 
- SSRF-SAFE fetch is mandatory: https/http only; resolve + REFUSE private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP ranges (127/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 169.254/16, ::1, fc00::/7); cap response size (~2MB) + timeout (~10s); follow max ~3 redirects re-validating each hop; send a normal descriptive User-Agent and respect an obvious robots disallow.
- The subdomain-deploy action is WIRED BUT GATED/INERT: it must not actually provision anything unless a real agency hosting target + domain are configured (they are NOT — agency.revsports.ca is a placeholder). Default = produce a deployable static bundle + mark DEPLOYED_STUB; only attempt real provisioning behind an explicit `AGENCY_DEPLOY_ENABLED` setting that is OFF by default. No live infra touched during build/staging.
- Keep the Phase 1 legal guardrails in generated demos (name-in-type, "not affiliated" disclaimer, noindex).
- No outreach sending.

=== PHASE 2 DELIVERABLES ===
1) Real scrape→extract: lib/agency/scrape.ts — SSRF-safe fetch of a prospect's currentSiteUrl, extract business name, tagline/headings, services, contact info, and a color hint from inline styles/meta (dependency-light HTML parsing; no headless browser). Feed extracted content into generateSiteIR to raise demo quality (the LLM gets real context; still degrades gracefully without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY). Store the raw extraction on the DemoSite/Prospect. Wire a "Scrape & generate" action on the prospect/demo pages.
2) Agency CRM / pipeline: extend AgencyProspect into a deal pipeline (stages: LEAD → CONTACTED → DEMO_SENT → NEGOTIATING → WON → LOST; add fields as needed — additive), a pipeline/kanban view at /admin/agency/pipeline, notes/activity log per prospect, and a client conversion (WON → an AgencyClient with the project + a simple proposal/quote: line items + total). If the platform has an invoice system, link a quote to it where trivial; otherwise keep quotes self-contained. 
3) Subdomain deploy pipeline (gated): lib/agency/deploy.ts — produce a self-contained static bundle from a DemoSite's renderedHtml, compute the intended slug.agency.revsports.ca host, and a deploy action that (a) OFF by default just records the bundle + DEPLOYED_STUB, (b) when AGENCY_DEPLOY_ENABLED is set, enqueues a real deploy via the existing hosting/vhost mechanism (reuse whatever the platform already uses for static sites; do not invent new infra). Document the enable steps.
4) UI: update /admin/agency pages for the pipeline, scrape action, quotes, and deploy status. Server actions in lib/actions-agency.ts (each re-checks requireArea("platform")). Match admin look; sentence case.
5) Tests: SSRF guard (private-IP refusal, redirect re-validation, size/timeout), extraction parsing, pipeline transitions, quote math. Update docs/DOCUMENTATION.md ("Sitewave — Phase 2").

When done: prisma generate + npm run build clean; commit + push; report files added/changed, models/fields added, the SSRF protections implemented, build/test result, and the staging command `cd /opt/nxeon && bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh feature/agency-sitewave-phase2`. Do not deploy.

1	# Marketing Agency — Architecture & Build Plan
2	
3	**Author:** Research/architecture agent · **Date:** 2026-08-10
4	**Status:** Research + planning only. No code written, nothing deployed, no APIs mutated.
5	
6	---
7	
8	## 1. Product Overview
9	
10	A **productized web-design agency as software**. Two halves:
11	
12	1. **Demo-Gen Engine (flagship, the wedge):** Pick a business vertical (dentist, restaurant, gym, law firm, salon, HVAC, med-spa, auto shop…) → load a vertical-specific site template → take a target business from a prospect list → scrape/read its *current* website → extract brand (logo, colors, copy, services, hours, reviews) → generate a demonstrably *better* AI-built site → deploy it to a per-prospect subdomain (`joes-diner.demos.agency-domain.com`) → hand the link to the **Cold Email Engine** (separate product) for outreach: *"We built you a free redesign — here it is."* When they click, a **claim/CTA flow** captures the warm lead.
13	2. **Agency CRM / Pipeline:** Once a prospect replies, the demo becomes a deal. Pipeline (Lead → Demo Sent → Opened → Replied → Call → Won → Onboarding → Live → Retainer), proposals/contracts, billing, and handoff (promote the demo to a real, owned site).
14	
15	It ships **standalone** (`agency.<domain>`) *and* as a **Nxeon admin add-on module** (`/admin/agency`), because Nxeon is the central hub and already owns the hosting infra the demos deploy onto.
16	
17	### Core value chain
18	`Vertical + Template Library` × `AI Generation` × `Cheap per-prospect Deploy` × `Personalized Outreach` = high-conversion lead-gen. The moat is **volume + personalization + the demo already exists** — the prospect sees the finished product, not a pitch.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## 2. Competitors & Positioning
23	
24	| Product | What it is | Price | Relevance |
25	|---|---|---|---|
26	| **Durable** | GPT-driven 30-sec site builder for local service businesses | ~$12–15/mo | Closest to our *generation* quality bar; all-in-one but generic templates. |
27	| **B12** | AI site in ~60s + human-assisted service tier | $42–$399/mo | Hybrid AI+expert; our "won client" tier competes here. |
28	| **10Web** | AI → full WordPress + managed hosting, Elementor editor | $10–20/mo+ | Proves AI→editable→hosted pipeline; WP lock-in. |
29	| **Framer AI / v0 (Vercel)** | AI generates high-design React/Framer sites | v0 $20/mo (5k credits); Framer usage-based | Best-in-class *output quality*; not an agency/outreach engine. |
30	| **Readdy / LeadGen.ai / ManyRequests-style "spec site" plays** | Auto-generate a personalized demo per lead + link it in outreach | agency SaaS pricing | **Direct competitor to our exact play** — validates the model. |
31	
32	**Positioning:** We are *not* selling a DIY builder. We sell **done-for-you demos at scale that convert cold prospects**, backed by a real agency pipeline + Nxeon hosting. Differentiators: (a) **per-vertical designed template library** (not generic), (b) **real brand extraction** from the prospect's existing site so the demo feels bespoke, (c) **owned hosting** = near-zero marginal deploy cost, (d) integrated CRM→billing→handoff, (e) tight loop with the Cold Email Engine.
33	
34	Sources: NxCode AI-builder roundup, fahimai 10Web-vs-B12, G2/B12 pricing, v0/Framer reviews, Readdy/LeadGen.ai agency pages (see §12).

58	## 4. Recommended Tech Stack
59	
60	- **Framework:** Next.js 15 App Router + TypeScript (matches Nxeon exactly; shares `components/portal/Shell.tsx`, `components/ui/`, `app/globals.css` design system).
61	- **DB:** PostgreSQL + Prisma. Standalone gets its own DB; as add-on, additive tables in the Nxeon schema (prefix `agency_` / `Agency*` models, mirroring how shared-hosting added `HostingNode`/`HostingAccount` without touching the VPS models).
62	- **Generation:** Anthropic SDK with **structured output** (JSON Schema / tool-use) to emit a validated **Site IR** (page → sections → blocks with typed props), *not* raw HTML. Deterministic renderer maps IR → React components from the vertical template. This is the 2026 best practice (structured output over free-form HTML — Outlines/tool-use) and keeps output on-brand and safe.
63	- **Rendering the demo:** Two options — (A) **static export** of the generated site (Next static/HTML) served as a plain vhost on a Nxeon shared node (cheapest, safest, no runtime); (B) a single multi-tenant Next app that renders by subdomain from stored IR. **MVP = (A) static export** (near-zero cost, trivially cacheable, no per-demo process).
64	- **Background work:** a worker/queue mirroring Nxeon's `HostingTask`/worker-tick pattern (jobs: `SCRAPE`, `GENERATE`, `RENDER`, `DEPLOY`, `SCREENSHOT`, `NOTIFY_OUTREACH`). Status-driven state machine so a demo self-completes and retries.
65	- **Storage:** generated assets + screenshots to disk/object store; IR JSON in Postgres.

77	                   extractedCopy(json), services(json), hours, reviews(json),
78	                   currentScreenshotUrl, rawScrape(json), extractedAt
79	Demo               id, prospectId, templateId, siteIR(json), status(enum),
80	                   subdomain, deployUrl, screenshotUrl, version,

94	## 6. Generation Pipeline (step by step)
95	
96	1. **Intake.** Prospect added (CSV import, Google Places pull, or handed over by Cold Email Engine). Assign vertical (heuristic on Places category + LLM classifier fallback).
97	2. **Scrape.** Fetch current site: Playwright (MVP) or Firecrawl `/scrape`. Capture HTML, full-page screenshot, and (Firecrawl `/extract` or Brandfetch) structured brand: **logo, palette, fonts, headings, services, hours, address, phone, review snippets**. Respect robots/ToS (§11). Store `BrandProfile`.
98	3. **Normalize + classify.** Cheap Haiku call: confirm vertical, summarize services, pull a value-prop, flag if the current site is missing (a *no-site* prospect is an even better target — generate from Places data only).
99	4. **Plan.** Sonnet call with **structured output** → **Site IR**: choose sections from the vertical template's `sectionCatalog` (hero, services grid, about, testimonials, gallery, booking CTA, map, FAQ, footer), write on-brand copy, map extracted colors→theme tokens (with contrast/accessibility guardrails), pick imagery. Validate IR against JSON Schema; reject/repair invalid.
100	5. **Render.** Deterministic renderer: IR + template React components + theme tokens → **static HTML/CSS** export. No prospect logo re-hosted verbatim if legal flag set — use their name in brand type + a neutral/generated mark (§11). Inject a discreet **"Demo by <Agency> — not affiliated with <Business>"** disclaimer + a **claim CTA**.
101	6. **QA gate.** Automated checks: valid HTML, Lighthouse/perf, no broken links, contrast, no profanity/hallucinated claims, required disclaimer present. Optional human-approve queue before it can be sent.
102	7. **Deploy.** Provision subdomain on Nxeon (§7), publish static files, issue SSL, warm cache. Store `deployUrl`.
103	8. **Screenshot before/after.** Render a side-by-side (their old site vs. our new) for the outreach email.
104	9. **Hand to Cold Email Engine.** Emit `demo.ready` webhook/event with `{prospect, deployUrl, beforeAfterImg, claimUrl}`. Cold Email Engine owns sending. We only track opens/clicks via the claim link + a tracking pixel/redirect we host.
105	10. **Warm-lead capture.** Claim page (`/claim/<token>`) = "Love it? Book a call / make it yours." Fires `DemoEvent` → creates/advances a `Deal`.
106	11. **Lifecycle.** Demos **auto-expire** (e.g. 30 days) and are torn down to reclaim subdomains and reduce brand-exposure risk unless converted.

155	## 10. Key Risks
156	
157	1. **Legal/brand exposure (biggest)** — see §11. Unsolicited use of a business's logo/brand in a live public demo is the single largest risk; mitigations are mandatory, not optional.
158	2. **Email deliverability & spam law** — outreach volume can nuke sending domains and trip CAN-SPAM/GDPR/CASL. Owned by Cold Email Engine, but our demo links/domains share reputation; keep demo domain separate from sending domain, honor opt-out, throttle.
159	3. **Generation quality variance** — a bad demo hurts the brand and the pitch. Mitigate with QA gate + human approve early + structured IR (not free HTML).
160	4. **Cost blow-ups** — Firecrawl `/extract` and Opus can get pricey at volume; default to Playwright + Sonnet/Haiku + Batch; cap per-prospect spend.
161	5. **Hosting abuse/reputation** — many auto-generated sites on shared IPs can look spammy to Google Safe Browsing; use `noindex` on demos, `robots: disallow`, isolate demo IP from production customer IPs.
162	6. **Scraping breakage / anti-bot** — sites block scrapers; Firecrawl fallback + graceful "generate from Places data only."
163	7. **Multi-tenant data isolation** if sold to sub-agencies.

167	## 11. Legal / Ethical / Compliance (MANDATORY)
168	
169	- **Trademark — nominative fair use.** Using a business's **plain-text name** to identify them (in the demo + outreach) is generally defensible nominative fair use: (a) they can't be identified without the name, (b) use only as much as necessary, (c) do nothing implying sponsorship/endorsement. **Using their distinctive logo, exact font, or full color scheme is riskier** — courts treat visual branding as more likely to imply endorsement and as "more than necessary." **Rule:** default to *name in type + a neutral/AI-generated mark + a palette inspired-by (not identical)*; only re-host their actual logo with consent. (INTA, Chase Law, Nolo, Davis+Gilbert.)
170	- **Copyright.** Their site copy/images are their (or a third party's) copyright. Don't republish verbatim; **rewrite** copy (we do — it's a *redesign*) and use **our/licensed/generated imagery**, not scraped photos. Logos may also be copyrighted separately from TM.
171	- **Clear disclaimer on every demo:** *"Unofficial concept redesign created by <Agency>. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or an official site of <Business>."* — kills the endorsement inference.
172	- **noindex / robots disallow** on all demos so they never rank or get mistaken for the real site; auto-expire + teardown when not converted.
173	- **Anti-spam:** outreach must comply with **CAN-SPAM** (US: valid physical address, honor opt-out, no deceptive headers), **GDPR/PECR** (EU/UK: legitimate-interest/consent), **CASL** (Canada: consent). Enforced by Cold Email Engine, but we provide **opt-out/takedown** on the demo + a suppression/deny list honored before any generation.
174	- **Scraping ToS/robots.** Respect `robots.txt` and site ToS; scrape only public pages, low rate, identify a UA; prefer Places/Brandfetch (licensed) over deep scraping. Some jurisdictions/sites prohibit scraping — keep an allow/deny list and a kill switch.
175	- **Takedown SLA + audit log** of what we scraped, generated, deployed, and sent per prospect.

6036	## Sitewave (Marketing Agency) — Phase 1 (2026-08-10)
6037	
6038	A productized web-design agency shipped as a Nxeon admin add-on module. **"Sitewave" is a placeholder
6039	brand** (name, palette indigo `#4F46E5` + coral `#FB7185` + ink `#0B1020`, tagline "Websites that win you
6040	customers.", placeholder demo domain `agency.revsports.ca` — stored as config in `lib/agency/config.ts`,
6041	**not** resolved via DNS). Built on branch `feature/agency-sitewave-phase1`.
6042	
6043	**The Phase 1 loop.** Add a *prospect* (a target business — manual or CSV, **no scraping**), assign a
6044	*vertical*, then **Generate demo** → the generator writes a structured **Site IR** (JSON: hero copy,
6045	services, about, CTA, an inspired-by palette) constrained to the vertical's section schema, and a
6046	**deterministic renderer** turns the IR into a self-contained static HTML page. **Preview** it in a new tab.
6047	**Deploy to subdomain** is a Phase-1 **stub** (records the intended `slug.agency.revsports.ca` host, marks
6048	the demo `DEPLOYED_STUB` — no nginx/DNS/filesystem write). **Send to outreach** creates/links a Cold Email
6049	`Business` + `Contact` from the prospect (reuses the existing coldemail models) but **sends nothing**.
6050	
6051	**Generation (`lib/agency/generate.ts`).** Calls Claude via the platform `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
6052	(`lib/anthropic.ts` `askClaude`, model `claude-opus-4-8`) to emit the Site IR as JSON. **Degrades
6053	gracefully** exactly like `lib/marketing/draft-gen.ts`: with no key (or on any API/JSON error) it falls
6054	back to a deterministic per-vertical template fill, so a demo is **always** produced. All output is coerced
6055	through `coerceSiteIR` (`lib/agency/schema.ts`) which never throws — every field is defaulted, palette hex
6056	validated, service/testimonial counts clamped.
6057	
6058	**Legal guardrails baked into the renderer (`lib/agency/render.ts`).** Per architecture §11 (the biggest
6059	risk), every rendered demo — LLM or fallback — carries: the business **name in plain type only** (no
6060	re-hosted logo, ever), an **inspired-by palette** (never the business's exact brand), a visible
6061	**"Independent concept — not affiliated with {business}"** disclaimer in both the top banner and the footer,
6062	and `<meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">`. All IR-derived text is HTML-escaped; the renderer is
6063	pure + deterministic (no clock, no randomness, no network). It self-asserts the guardrails and
6064	`generateDemo` **refuses to persist** a demo that fails the assertion. The preview route also sends
6065	`X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`.
6066	
6067	**Schema additions (additive, all `Agency*`-prefixed — never touch VPS/hosting/coldemail models).**
6068	`AgencyVertical` (slug, name, description), `AgencyTemplate` (verticalId, name, JSON `structure` /
6069	section-schema), `AgencyProspect` (businessName, vertical, contactEmail?, currentSiteUrl?, pastedSiteText,
6070	notes, `status` enum `PROSPECT|GENERATED|SENT|WON|LOST`, outreachBusinessId?), `AgencyDemoSite` (prospectId,
6071	templateId?, `siteIR` Json, renderedHtml, slug, `status` enum `DRAFT|GENERATED|DEPLOYED_STUB`, `noindex`
6072	default true, intendedHost?, deployedAt?), and `AgencyGenerationLog` (demoId, mode `llm|fallback`, model,
6073	ok, message). Indexed on slug/status/vertical/createdAt/foreign keys. **Requires a migration before use —
6074	this branch does NOT run `prisma db push`.**
6075	
6076	**Starter template library (`lib/agency/templates.ts` + `prisma/seed-agency.ts`).** Five seeded verticals —
6077	dentist, restaurant, gym, law firm, salon — each with a section schema (hero, services, about, testimonials,
6078	contact) and deterministic fallback content. `templates.ts` is the single source of truth shared by the seed
6079	and the generator's fallback, so the DB library and the no-API path stay in lockstep. Seed manually:
6080	`NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging npx tsx prisma/seed-agency.ts`.
6081	
6082	**Admin surface** (new top-level **Agency** nav section, entry "Sitewave", icon `globe`; all routes map to
6083	area `platform` = ADMIN-only): `/admin/agency` (overview — counts + prospects-by-status + LLM-availability
6084	banner), `/admin/agency/verticals` (manage verticals + templates), `/admin/agency/prospects` (CRUD + CSV
6085	paste + Generate demo + Send to outreach), `/admin/agency/demos` (list + preview + deploy-stub). Preview
6086	serve route: `app/api/agency/demo/[id]/preview` (staff-gated, returns stored HTML with noindex headers).
6087	Server actions live in `lib/actions-agency.ts` — **every export re-checks `requireArea("platform")`**.
6088	
6089	**Phase 2 (documented, not built).** Real subdomain provisioning (reuse the shared-hosting name-based nginx
6090	vhost + certbot SNI sweep + Namecheap wildcard DNS), live scrape/brand-extract → BrandProfile, a QA gate +
6091	human-approve queue, a worker job/state-machine, and the `demo.ready` webhook to the Cold Email Engine with
6092	open/click/claim tracking. See `scratchpad/projects/agency/architecture.md` + `board.json`.
6093	
6094	**Guardrails honoured:** no real scraping, no outreach sending, no live provisioning, no `prisma db push`,
6095	no `.env` edit, no deploy, not committed to main. `npx prisma generate` + `npm run build` both clean; the
6096	new `test/agency-generate-render.test.ts` suite (15 tests) passes.
